v55g: v55d plus opponent-class branch tables. At step 2 the opponent is classed by its cash (public-chassis / animal-first leaders / low-cash / other); at step 144 the route is picked from a per-class table selected on that class's recent public replays and validated on a disjoint half. Held-out seeds, both seats: vs v55b 132-56 decisive, vs v55d 115-51; 122 fresh ladder games replayed with opponents' recorded actions: 91.0% (v55d 86.9%, v55b 82.0%).

v55d: v55b with 15 shop-combo branches replaced by better Arjun-replay branches (selected on held-out large seeds, validated on a disjoint set). Head-to-head vs v55b 58-40 decisive (256 games, both seats); exact counterfactual on v55b's 28 ladder games with opponents' recorded actions: 26 wins vs 23.

v55b: animal-first opening route table reconstructed from Arjun Vinod's public ladder replays (fixed opening, branch by first unlocked shop at step 72 and by first two shops at step 144; Kaggle staff confirmed building submissions from public replays is allowed), plus our own 8-step sell-lead layer (fertilizer included). Out-of-sample large seeds, both seats: vs the raw replayed route table 230/256, vs our previous best v54r38g 224/256, vs Master Engine 228/256. Stratified official replays (490 boards, opponents' recorded actions): 91% (v54r38g 63%); 300 of our own ladder games replayed: 95% (v54r38g 74%).

v54r38g: v54r38f with fertilizer added to the 8-step sell-lead layer (fertilizer is our highest-volume sale). Paired sequential sign tests vs r38f on three disjoint sets of out-of-sample large seeds (both seats, 5 strongest local agents): +13/-8, +12/-2 (p=0.006), +11/-2 (p=0.011); exact replay of our 322 ladder games with the opponents' recorded actions: 259 wins vs r38f 250.

v54r38f: v54r38e plus an outer sell-lead layer: premium goods (all but wheat/fertilizer) that the tape plans to sell within the next 8 steps are sold as soon as they are in the shed, and later planned sells are reduced accordingly (inspired by devasad67's public write-up; own implementation). Mirror opponents share our routes, so selling first wins the price race. Out-of-sample large seeds, both seats, 5 strongest local agents: 1035 and 1019 vs r38e 1009 (per 1280); sequential paired sign test on fresh seeds + official replays: +18/-7 flips, p=0.022; exact replay of our 322 ladder games: 250 wins vs r38e 244.

v54r38c: r38 with the animal-first row narrowed to the identified cluster (rival cash at t2 in 460-650). v54r17: emergency coverage of the new Herd-Safe family plus per-key row split. Dmitrii's Herd-Safe Sale Window = rescue7 + 21-line opening layer (BUY_PRODUCT WHEAT 8 / SELL 3); that single change moves the t2 rival fingerprint from (1042,9989) to (1046,9989), so our whole 40-cell table stopped firing against it (bench 53/128 = 41.4% vs 107/128 = 83.6% against rescue7). Fix: (a) add 1046 to the mirror-row and t216-layer key whitelist, (b) build a herdsafe-specific combo index and select 7 additional cells from its own weak combos, placed in a dedicated _V54R3_HS row that only fires on 1046 -- the shared-row variant (r16) gained 7 on herdsafe but lost 3/2/1 on rescue7/v54/v56 and was rejected by bench. Result: herdsafe 41.4% -> 74.2% with all five other families byte-identical. bench (6 rivals x 128 paired): 660/768 = 85.9% vs r14 618/768 = 80.5%. gate9 288/288.
